terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the candles file here: each line at the bottom tries one task and prints what came out, or the error it stopped with.

tasks.title: A card that sells itself
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/candles.js`, make `makeCard(name, stock)` return an object with the properties `name` and `stock`, and a method `sell(count)` that takes `count` off the `stock` property of the object it is called on, using `this`.

Check makes cards of its own and sells from them. It also changes a card's stock before selling, and calls `sell` on another object, to make sure `sell` works through `this`.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's parts on methods and on this.
Return an object with `name` and `stock` from `makeCard`.
Add `sell(count)` to it as a method, and change `this.stock` inside it.
Run the file: the first line should show the Fig card's stock after the sale.
hints: You returned an object of methods in the issue on helpers that remember. This time the stock is a property of the object, not a variable kept beside it.
Inside a method, `this` is the object before the dot of the call: in `card.sell(2)`, it is `card`. A method written with `=>` has no `this` of its own.
The object is `{ name, stock, sell(count) { this.stock = this.stock - count } }`.

tasks.title: A class for candles
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a class `Candle`, and export it. `new Candle(name, priceCents)` makes a candle with the properties `name` and `priceCents`, set from its parameters, and `stock`, set to `0`. It has three methods:

- `restock(count)` adds `count` to its stock
- `sell(count)` takes `count` off its stock
- `label()` gives `'Sage: 2 left'`, or `'Sage: sold out'` when its stock is `0`

Check makes candles of its own with `new`, restocks and sells from them, reads their labels, and reads your file for the class and its export.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on classes.
Write `export class Candle {` and its closing brace.
Inside, write the constructor first, then the three methods.
Run the file: the Sage line should show its label.
hints: Every property a candle has gets its first value in the constructor, `stock` included, so a candle is whole the moment it is made.
Inside the class, `this` is the candle the method was called on, or the new candle in the constructor. The methods are written like the `sell` of Task 1, with no commas between them.
The constructor sets `this.name = name`, `this.priceCents = priceCents` and `this.stock = 0`; `label()` starts ``if (this.stock === 0) { return `${this.name}: sold out` }``.

tasks.title: A limited edition, built on Candle
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, write a class `LimitedCandle`, built on `Candle` with `extends`, and export it. `new LimitedCandle(name, priceCents, edition)` makes a candle the way `Candle` does, and also has the property `edition`. Its `label()` gives the label of `Candle`, then `, limited to ` and the edition: `'Snow: 3 left, limited to 20'`. Use the label of `Candle` for the first part. `restock` and `sell` come from `Candle`, unchanged.

Check makes limited candles of its own, reads their labels, restocks and sells from them, and changes the label of `Candle` to make sure the limited label uses it.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on one class built on another.
Write `export class LimitedCandle extends Candle {` and its closing brace.
In its constructor, let `Candle` make the candle first, then set `edition`.
Write `label()`, using the label of `Candle`, and run the file.
hints: A class built on another has every method of the first. It only writes what is new or different: here, the constructor and the label.
`super(...)` runs the constructor of `Candle`, and must come before any use of `this`. `super.label()` gives the label `Candle` would give.
The constructor is `super(name, priceCents)` then `this.edition = edition`; `label()` returns `` `${super.label()}, limited to ${this.edition}` ``.

tasks.title: Sell when the payment comes in
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, make `sellOnPayment(candle, order)` hand `whenPaid` a handler that sells from `candle` the number of candles it is called with, so they are taken off its stock once the order is paid. Leave `whenPaid` as it is.

Check calls `sellOnPayment` with a candle of its own, and with a till that is paid later, to make sure nothing is sold before the payment comes in.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on passing a method.
Call `whenPaid` with the order and a handler.
Make sure that when the handler runs, `sell` is called on the candle.
Run the file: the Amber line should show the stock after the payment.
hints: `whenPaid` calls the handler by itself, as `handler(order.qty)`, with nothing before the dot.
Handing over `candle.sell` passes the method on its own: when `whenPaid` calls it, `this` is `undefined`. A small arrow function of your own can call `sell` on the candle.
